passage: You asked about the topper in our class? That's Ishita. Honestly, I used to be jealous. Then I sat next to her in the physics exam. She got 49 out of 50, and her hands started shaking. She kept saying, "I lost a mark on units. Units!" Some people rolled their eyes, like, "Oh no, poor you." But she wasn't showing off. She looked scared. So I did something small. I said, "That's an amazing score. Want to get pani puri after school? No maths talk allowed." She stared at me like nobody had ever asked. We went. She laughed so hard at the stall. I think she's kind of lonely up there, you know? Anyway, I'm Arohi, and now we get pani puri every Friday.

qa.q: What did Ishita score in the physics exam?
qa.a: She got 49 out of 50.

qa.q: How did Arohi's feelings about Ishita change after the physics exam?
qa.a: Arohi went from feeling jealous to feeling concerned, seeing that Ishita looked scared rather than proud.

qa.q: What choice did Arohi make, and why did it help Ishita?
qa.a: Arohi praised the score kindly and invited Ishita for pani puri with no maths talk, which eased her isolation.

qa.q: How might Ishita have felt being invited for pani puri?
qa.a: She seemed surprised, as if nobody had asked before, and then relieved enough to laugh.

grounding: A classmate notices the topper can't enjoy a near-perfect score, answers with kindness instead of eye-rolling and invites her to relax.

passage: I'm Rafiq, from 11B. Kashish has topped every exam since class eight, and some of the boys at the back call her "the machine". I used to laugh along. Then last Tuesday, after the chemistry test, I found her in the empty lab, redoing a question she'd already got right, lips moving. She'd scored 98. When I said, "Congrats," she flinched and said, "That's two marks gone." She didn't look happy at all. I don't really know what she feels. But I stopped laughing at the machine jokes. Yesterday I asked if she wanted to join our Saturday cricket, just to bowl badly with us. She said maybe.

qa.q: What did Kashish score in the chemistry test?
qa.a: She scored 98.

qa.q: What did Rafiq seem to feel after finding Kashish in the empty lab?
qa.a: Rafiq seems concerned for Kashish and sorry for laughing along, which is why the machine jokes stopped being funny and the cricket invitation came.

qa.q: What choices did Rafiq make after seeing Kashish in the lab?
qa.a: Rafiq stopped laughing at the "machine" jokes and invited Kashish to Saturday cricket, offering kindness and a way to relax.

qa.q: How might Kashish feel being invited to bowl badly at Saturday cricket?
qa.a: Kashish might feel surprised and a little lighter, since someone saw more than the marks; 'maybe' suggests cautious interest.

grounding: A classmate sees a topper anxious over two marks, stops joining the teasing and invites her to relax with the group.

passage: When I was fifteen, beta, there was a boy in my class called Raghav who topped every exam. Everyone disliked him a little for it. I did too, at first. Then one day he got 89 in biology, and I found him crying behind the chemistry lab, saying his father would ask about the eleven marks. I didn't know what to say. So I, Payal, who had got 61, sat next to him and said, "Eighty-nine is more than I'll ever get." He laughed, wet-faced. After that I stopped calling him "topper" and started inviting him to our Sunday cricket. He was terrible at it. He laughed more than I'd ever heard. We're still friends, you know. He's the uncle who brings you mangoes.

qa.q: What did Raghav get in biology?
What did young Payal feel on finding Raghav crying?
qa.a: Payal felt surprised and unsure what to say, and moved to comfort him instead of resenting him.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story?
qa.a: Payal sat with Raghav, then stopped calling him topper and invited him to Sunday cricket.

qa.q: How did Raghav experience being included in the cricket?
qa.a: He relaxed and laughed more than ever, feeling less alone despite being terrible at the game.

grounding: Shows a classmate who stops resenting a topper, notices his anxiety over marks and invites him to relax.

passage: The class-trip bus broke down on the ghat road in pouring rain, and everyone groaned, then started singing antakshari. Everyone except Harsha, the class topper, who sat at the back with a chemistry guide open on her knees, lips moving. Ira watched her for a while. Some boys joked that Harsha would study at her own wedding. Ira didn't laugh. She'd seen Harsha's hands shake last week when a test came back with one mark cut. Ira slid into the seat beside her. "We need one more for our team, and you know all the old songs." Harsha glanced at the book. "I have a test on Monday." "It'll still be there in ten minutes." Harsha closed it, slowly, and joined in on the second song.

qa.q: Where did the bus break down?
qa.a: On the ghat road, in pouring rain.

qa.q: What was Ira thinking as she watched Harsha study?
qa.a: Ira felt concerned, remembering Harsha's shaking hands over one lost mark, and didn't find the jokes funny.

qa.q: Why was Ira's invitation a good approach?
qa.a: It was kind and light, didn't mock Harsha's success and gave her a small, safe reason to relax.

qa.q: How might Harsha feel when she closes the book?
qa.a: Harsha may feel nervous about the test but relieved to be included and to take a break.

grounding: Illustrates a peer noticing a topper's anxiety, not mocking her success and inviting her to relax.

passage:
Results were pinned up outside the staff room in their Jaipur school. Kishore was first again, 98.5 per cent. Madhav was fifteenth and fine with it.
But Kishore wasn't celebrating. He was staring at the physics column, lips moving. "I lost one mark on a unit. One mark."
Some boys behind them muttered, "Topper's crying over 99, poor thing." Madhav felt a flash of annoyance at them, and something else at Kishore's face: worry.
He waited until the others left. "Hey. You did amazing. Seriously."
Kishore shrugged. "It should've been full."
"Want to come to the cricket ground after school? No studying allowed."
Kishore hesitated. "I have to redo that chapter."
"One hour. Then redo it."
After a moment, Kishore half-smiled. "One hour."

qa.q: What percentage did Kishore get?
qa.a: 98.5 per cent.

qa.q: What was Madhav feeling as he watched Kishore's face?
qa.a: Madhav felt annoyed at the boys who mocked Kishore, and worried about how anxious Kishore looked over one mark.

qa.q: Which of Madhav's choices could make Kishore feel less alone?
qa.a: Praising him sincerely instead of joining the mocking, and inviting him to the cricket ground for an hour with no studying.

qa.q: What might it be like for Kishore to hear "Topper's crying over 99"?
qa.a: It may make Kishore feel lonely and misunderstood, since others see only his success and not how anxious he is.

grounding: Shows a classmate noticing a topper who cannot enjoy results, choosing kindness over mocking and inviting him to relax.
